approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from a bounded population of accepted, scored molecules. It samples breeding parents from high-score bands, recombines connected fragments, and applies ordinary graph mutations and continuation walks; direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled. Stable canonical admission creates a fresh surplus pool. A Gaussian process fitted to every earlier accepted score uses counts of local molecular environments and generalized Tanimoto similarity. It draws one correlated score function for each announced batch position and takes each masked maximum, without conditioning later draws on earlier selections. Only real accepted feedback updates its prediction archive and score-ranked breeding population.
approach.novelty: Add the previously tested mean-fantasy residual projection to this exchange-free Parent. After each choice, project later random residuals as if that pending molecule equaled its current predicted mean, keeping the means and fitted model unchanged. This is an exact transfer of an existing rule, not a new conditioning formula or a demonstrated improvement: its earlier trial under an exchange-containing Parent changed many batches but slightly lowered the final mean. Current siblings have removed residual correlation, optimized a shared sampled batch maximum, or reserved the last position for conditional variance. None tests this unchanged zero-innovation projection in the present composition. The experiment asks whether its changed later choices now help complete search outcomes; contraction, local parent wins and accepted reuse alone cannot answer that.

observed_bottleneck: The specific Parent behavior is uncoordinated later residual draws within an otherwise covariance-aware batch: n-62daf219c70a uses independent rows of one original joint-normal draw matrix, with only exact identity masking between positions. Its source makes no pending-location residual projection. Its published baseline audit reconstructs all 435 fitted selections with nonzero off-diagonal posterior covariance, 3755 choices away from the available mean maximum, and 629 strict best-generating-parent beats among 4350 accepted offspring; 258 incumbent improvements and 2401 later-used breeding identities show an active but uneven feedback chain, not a proven redundancy cause. The actual three summary.json and run.log files are complete and successful, with macros 0.625411930168826, 0.560865654270234 and 0.600731364761313, mean 0.5956696497334577 and population SD 0.02659287062806747. This motivates testing one source-defined batch coordination opportunity without claiming that it explains the dispersion. The exact archived n-521f362b3777 rule on n-559d25e9c9c7 already executed all 3915 projections, preserved 435 first choices, changed 600 positions and 287 batch sets, and increased local parent beats from 624 to 677, yet lost paired macro mean 0.0018442146149799665 with seed deltas [-0.025832907146107975, 0.030006461504202053, -0.009706198203033978]. Its historical mean contraction was only 3.30% and its median 0.81%; lower model correlation was not universal chemical diversification or benefit. Current-Parent correlation removal n-54adc6a641e8 loses 0.018447481386582327, supporting retention of the original covariance, not this added projection. Current distinct objectives n-062b351ccb52 and n-8a62df15e51f lose 0.022789878982636996 and 0.05627557001043134 despite exposed selection and predictive effects. These adverse results remain counterevidence to treating model uncertainty, local wins or learning activity as endpoint utility.
hypothesis: Add the exact archived mean-fantasy within-batch residual projection to the exchange-disabled Parent: condition future sampled residual rows on each earlier selected molecule taking its unchanged posterior mean, using the original jittered sampling covariance and zero innovations only for batch allocation.

finding_summary.headline: Projection changed batch choices, but endpoint score fell on all three seeds
finding_summary.insights: The result rules out nonactivation, missing accepted feedback or numerical fallback as explanations for the failed endpoint prediction. Lower average model correlation, selected-stream prediction error and seed dispersion were insufficient to improve search. The slightly larger count of parent wins partly accompanies weaker generating parents, so it does not establish higher absolute quality. Downstream opportunity also had limits: three newly selected nonterminal molecules had positive breeding support but were never drawn; four task/seed cohorts of new selections produced no positive direct-descendant incumbent increment, while terminal selections had no later opportunity. The earlier trial under an exchange-containing Parent was also adverse; this complete loss ends the registered fixed transfer without parameter rescue. The molecular assessment still finds chemically varied aromatic and heterocyclic outputs, alongside reactive halogen bonds, difficult ring geometry and unspecified stereochemistry. Those liabilities and inconsistent useful family coverage remain relevant gaps, but these data do not identify chemical mediation, an exchange interaction or the contribution of the retained graph-evolution foundation.
finding_summary.results: All 3,915 projections executed correctly and preserved every first choice. They changed 657 later positions and 295 of 435 batch sets, replacing 493 selected memberships. Later selected sampling variance fell by 3.28% on average. These choices entered real feedback: all 482 nonterminal newly selected molecules entered later fits, and 296 of the 493 new selections later bred. Yet the final mean fell from 0.595670 to 0.553927, a paired loss of 0.041742 against the required gain of 0.002. All three seed macros fell; six task/seed endpoints improved and nine declined. Strict parent wins rose from 629 to 642, while absolute offspring mean fell from 0.385256 to 0.359834 and total incumbent improvement fell from 5.807663 to 5.181529. The largest endpoint losses were deco_hop in seed 0 and sitagliptin_mpo in seed 2; median_2 improved in two seeds but fell in the third.

molecular.headline: Aromatic and nitrogen-rich rings recur, with reactive halogen bonds, difficult ring geometry and unspecified stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: Node n-aa9acd2c2043 produces compact indole carboxamides, linked nitrogen/oxygen heterocycles, aryl-substituted cyclic and acyclic amines, diaryl amino-lactams, and fluorinated imino/carbonyl rings. Ring formation, aromatic chemistry and basic amine centres are clearly available. The missing capabilities are consistent local bond plausibility, credible ring geometry, stereochemical specification, and reliable access to plausible alternatives within a successful chemical family. These are output observations, not an attribution to the allocation rule. Recognizable medicinal chemistry coexists with N-F, N-Cl, N-Br, O-F, peroxide and unusual ring environments, so graph validity does not justify a strong drug-likeness or synthetic-plausibility judgement. Across the five tasks the digest ring-closure-string incidence is 0.9621 to 0.9862 and aromatic-string incidence is 0.8678 to 0.9713. These are molecule-level text incidences, not ring counts or aromatic-atom fractions. Charge and stereocentre-string incidence is 0.0 throughout; neutral drawings still contain protonatable amines, and several saturated centres are potentially stereogenic. Diversity is moderate across seeds and tasks, with narrower leading families within several seeds; the record also contains substantial ring-topology variation and does not show global scaffold collapse. All fifteen Child and fifteen published Parent n-62daf219c70a trajectory files were present and read: 4500 observations per panel, including 4350 optimizer proposals per panel. Each task has 900 observations and 870 optimizer proposals. No task or supplied seed comparison is absent. context.comparison separately reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true, matched seeds 0, 1 and 2, and no profile mismatch. The per-task comparisons below use those current Child and Parent trajectories. The earlier gap provenance in n-c55c3d520a2c is retained as reported in the indexed Parent assessment; its historical profile is not pooled into this comparison. All cited_smiles are exact Child trajectory strings authorized by this brief. Heavy-atom and local-bond descriptions were derived offline from the supplied molecular graphs; the supporting source hashes, descriptor definitions and all seed summaries are in .slots/round-0025-slot-1/molecular-trajectory-audit.json, with row-level descriptors in .slots/round-0025-slot-1/molecular-descriptors.jsonl. These computations add no oracle scores. The digest final_molecules are late seed-2 proposals, not each seed's retained best molecule; full trajectories establish the seed-specific examples below. Observed scores do not establish synthesis, stability, binding, an exact missing pharmacophore, or chemical mediation of an algorithmic effect.

per_task.generated_character: The proposal median is 25 heavy atoms. Seed 0 leads with a 25-heavy-atom substituted indole anilide carrying phenol, an N-fluoro indole and an N-bromo methylamino substituent. Seed 2 also reaches 25-heavy-atom indole carboxamides, with methoxy, methyl and halomethylamino substitution, but puts fluorine directly on the amide nitrogen. Seed 1 instead favors a 24-heavy-atom, pyridyl-substituted fused diaza-lactam with an N-N bond and a small carbonyl ring; its leader has a thiomethyl side chain and no halogen. These are compact aromatic frameworks, not ring-poor output. Ordinary amide and heteroaryl chemistry is recognizable, but the N-halogen and small N-N-containing ring environments make synthesis and stability questionable. The digest halogen-string incidence is 0.9287; the halogen-free seed-1 family is an important exception. Parent seeds retain related aromatic amide/diketone or amino-cumulene families, rather than an entirely different chemistry class.
liabilities: N-F on indole or amide nitrogen and N-Br/N-Cl on an amino substituent are distinct from ordinary carbon-bound aromatic halogens and raise local reactivity concerns.
The alternative fused diaza-lactam contains an N-N bond and a small carbonyl ring; its score does not establish accessible synthesis or geometry.
Late tiny fragments and much larger duplicate-like assemblies can discard the favorable functional-group context despite syntactically valid SMILES.
missing_features: The leading aromatic-amide families do not consistently realize their useful arrangement with conventional stable nitrogen substitution. The initial N-H indole amide and the halogen-free seed-1 family show that such chemistry is available, so the gap is reliability rather than absolute inability.
Plausible independent compact frameworks are limited among the leading seed-local examples; peripheral halogen and short-side-chain changes often preserve the same family.
The observed score ordering does not identify an exact missing target motif or demonstrate that more rings, halogens or nitrogen atoms would help.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The common initial trimethoxyindole anilide scores 0.3051048083696145. Child seed leaders score 0.4182215872091703, 0.42348216717712805 and 0.4478476056206344 for seeds 0, 1 and 2, respectively; the matched Parent values are 0.39405142067435733, 0.47411701813450596 and 0.438972502037081. Thus the Child's distinct small-ring seed-1 family accompanies a lower endpoint, while the other two seed endpoints are higher. In seed 2, changing the leader's N-fluoromethyl side group to N-bromomethyl leaves the score at 0.4478476056206344. The halogen-free seed-1 leader and its methyl-side-chain relative score 0.42348216717712805 and 0.4123376517249664. A much larger duplicated indole-amide assembly at seed-2 evaluation 25 scores 4.958781512190985e-10, and isolated F scores 0.0. The observed association favors a compact, combined aromatic/carbonyl arrangement over either severe fragmentation or duplicated elaboration. It does not isolate an N-halogen requirement or reward halogen identity consistently.

per_task.generated_character: This is the largest Child proposal population: median 39 heavy atoms versus 33 in the Parent, with highly substituted linked and fused heterocycles. Seed 1 leads with a 41-heavy-atom assembly of oxygen/nitrogen carbonyl heterocycles linked through a phenyl ether/aryl connection, methoxy and fluoromethyl groups, and a fused small oxygen ring. Seed 0 instead reaches a 28-heavy-atom, densely bridged aza-aromatic graph with an alkynyl ether/imine side chain. Seed 2 reaches a 38-heavy-atom diaryl nitrogen-rich carbonyl-thione system with several imine segments and an aromatic-labelled nine-membered ring. Ring and aromatic-string incidences are 0.9736 and 0.9713. These are substantially different seed families, although each leading group is locally concentrated. The seed-1 leader has no N-halogen or O-halogen bond, unlike the Parent's leading seed-0 family; that is a real local chemical counterexample, not proof of general synthetic accessibility.
liabilities: Lowercase aromatic notation in the densely bridged aza graphs and the nine-membered nitrogen ring does not establish a planar, stable aromatic structure.
Alkynyl ethers, repeated imine environments, carbonyl-thione substitution and fused small oxygen rings make these more demanding synthetic targets than a ring count suggests.
Very large repeated heterocyclic assemblies add complexity without reproducing the best observed values; their distinct strings are not evidence of useful independent scaffold coverage.
missing_features: The Child does not consistently recover the compact linked heterocyclic organization accompanying the stronger Parent seed-0 score; it instead explores a different dense aza-cage family. This is observed chemical coverage, not an attribution of score loss to one motif.
Geometrically credible, synthetically supported alternatives to the aromatic-labelled cages, large nitrogen ring and small fused oxygen ring are not demonstrated by these records.
The output lacks reliable control of elaboration while preserving favorable linked functional-group context; neither a fixed minimum size nor more rings follows from this gradient.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Child seed leaders score 0.612781954887218, 0.626750700280112 and 0.6048290937996821, against Parent values 0.8561477222467935, 0.6248206599713055 and 0.6178024026512013. The Parent's compact linked aza-heterocycle/carbonyl-thione arrangement in seed 0 is therefore not recovered at a comparable observed score by the Child's different aza-cage family. In Child seed 1, the smaller methoxy-substituted fused carbonyl/nitrile molecule at evaluation 125 scores 0.5263201871657754, while the linked leader reaches 0.626750700280112. Yet the much larger related assembly at evaluation 299 scores 0.6146288209606987, and the largest 113-heavy-atom proposal at evaluation 225 scores 0.5845735884715332. Ethene scores 0.5. Thus combined heterocyclic organization is associated with higher values, but simple size, ring proliferation or retention of the same local fragments is insufficient. The floor value 0.5 is not evidence of useful chemistry, and the much better Parent seed-0 record does not establish that its reactive O-F substituent causes its advantage.

per_task.generated_character: Accessible aliphatic amines combined with aromatic surface dominate the strong examples. Seed 2 leads with a 23-heavy-atom N-propylpyrrolidine attached to a fluoroindane bearing a chloro-N-methylaziridinyl substituent. A 19-heavy-atom relative retains the pyrrolidine and substituted indane without that extra small nitrogen ring. Seed 0 favors a 22-heavy-atom fused unsaturated tertiary amine with aminoalkyl and fluoro-phenol substitution. Seed 1 reaches a larger 34-heavy-atom cyclobutyl aryl-diamine connected to a dichloroaryl sulfoxide. Median proposal size is 26 heavy atoms versus 31 for the Parent, which leads with flexible diaryl tertiary amines and cyclic-amine/fused-thioether families. These recognizable amines offer more conventional synthetic handles than several other task leaders, although their substituted small rings and stereochemical ambiguity remain material. The digest halogen-string incidence is 0.9793.
liabilities: The leading chloro-aziridine combines a small strained nitrogen ring and carbon-bound chlorine; its near-ceiling score does not certify stability or synthetic convenience.
The larger diamine/sulfoxide family combines several flexible connections, halogen substitution and potentially stereogenic carbon/sulfur environments without defined stereochemistry.
Halogenated aminoalkyl groups and dense ring junctions need local assessment; the simpler high-scoring indane/pyrrolidine is a counterexample to treating all strong candidates as equally problematic.
missing_features: Stereochemically specified versions of the substituted pyrrolidine/indane, bicyclic amine and small-ring families are absent despite potentially stereogenic centres.

Consistent access to a simple amine/aromatic arrangement at similarly high values across seeds is not established; the compact seed-2 relative demonstrates that some simplification is already possible.
Explicit protonation-state assignments are absent, but basic centres are clearly present in the neutral strings. These molecules do not support guidance simply to add an amine or a nitrogen ring.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Child seed leaders score 0.9867083943787386, 0.9738494501614986 and 0.9999959962849514; Parent values are 0.9999989177995104, 0.9969753164881906 and 0.9999934235240012. The very high seed-2 Child value therefore does not summarize seeds 0 and 1. The seed-2 relative without the chloro-aziridine appendage scores 0.9999918570022562, showing that this liability and maximal size are unnecessary for a near-ceiling score in the visible sample. A chlorinated sulfoxide fragment without an amine scores 0.00014259210235230567, and an acid/amide/N-sulfonyl-pyrrolidine structure scores 0.0006269216484658979. The seed-0 late relative lacking the pendant amino group scores 0.6455179577104256, below the 0.9867083943787386 leader, though other substituents differ as well. These comparisons associate useful scores with the combined presentation of available amines and aromatic regions, not with nitrogen count or halogen count alone. They are supplied scores, not measured affinity or a causal estimate for an individual functional group.

per_task.generated_character: The Child produces medium-sized aromatic/nitrogen-carbonyl assemblies, with proposal median 32 heavy atoms versus 30 in the Parent. The 35-heavy-atom seed-0 leader joins two aryl groups to hydrazone-like N-N=C connectivity and fused medium-sized nitrogen rings containing carbonyls. The 33-heavy-atom seed-1 leader has a biphenyl-spanning aza-lactam connected through an exocyclic alkene to an N-methylpiperidone, with propyl and ethoxy substitution. Its graph contains a ten-membered ring. Seed 2 instead reaches a 32-heavy-atom quinoline/aminopyridine ether linked to an eight-membered cyclic urea containing additional amine functionality. Ring, aryl, ether, amine and carbonyl chemistry are all present. Halogen-string incidence is only 0.1046. The Parent also supplies quinoline-linked nitrogen/carbonyl rings and bridged diaryl lactams, so these remain related broad chemistry classes despite different connectivity and seed-specific outcomes.
liabilities: The biphenyl-spanning medium ring, exocyclic alkene and substituted saturated ring require geometry and stereochemical assessment beyond a valid graph.
Hydrazone-like N-N=C and nearby N-O/N-N variants create environment-specific stability questions; these do not make every amine or carbonyl undesirable.
Duplicated large assemblies can combine familiar fragments yet perform poorly, so functional-group inventory alone overstates chemical quality.
missing_features: Simpler, synthetically supported ways to retain the favorable aryl/amine/carbonyl relationships are not consistently demonstrated at the leading values; useful partial carbonyl simplification is already visible.

Stereochemical and conformational identity is unresolved for the substituted saturated and medium-ring examples. The relatively unbridged seed-2 ether/cyclic-urea family shows that difficult bridging is not universal.

The visible gradients do not identify an exact missing target pharmacophore. Ring and heteroatom richness are present, and the leading seed-2 structures also show varied connectivity rather than complete scaffold collapse.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Child seed leaders score 0.23358829607557838, 0.23650145514537424 and 0.22004784168807234, versus Parent values 0.2258403994203931, 0.2214095461892601 and 0.22600312875247064. The first two Child families therefore accompany higher endpoints, whereas the third does not. Methane scores 0.0, a simple fluoroacetanilide scores 0.07615914142616902, and a nitrogen-rich compact bridged carbonyl/acid structure without an aromatic region scores 0.07411449079956543. The common initial aryl fused dione scores 0.1678386594791329. Retaining both aromatic and nitrogen-carbonyl regions is associated with the stronger values. In seed 1, removing the piperidone carbonyl gives 0.22479304903314293, whereas removing the other carbonyl leaves 0.23186944788008412, close to the leader. This shows context-dependent carbonyl contributions, not a universal need to maximize them. A much larger 67-heavy-atom assembly scores 0.15517818003356154. The scores do not show that extra bridges, nitrogen atoms or general molecular size resolve the remaining gap.

per_task.generated_character: Fluorinated imino/carbonyl and dione heterocycles dominate, with median proposal size 26 heavy atoms. The 28-heavy-atom seed-0 leader is nonaromatic by graph perception: it combines an imino/carbonyl nitrogen ring, an unsaturated small aza ring, a fluorinated cyclopropene, a substituted cyclohexadiene, N-F bonds and an O-F-bearing carbonyl side chain. Seed 1 leads with another 28-heavy-atom structure containing an aromatic-labelled nine-membered nitrogen-dione ring, N-acetyl/N-fluoro substitution and a fluorinated cyclopentene. Seed 2 favors a 27-heavy-atom fused dione attached to a phenyl hydroxylamine/ethylthiol region, with carbon-bound fluorine and N-F. The digest aromatic-string incidence of 0.8678 therefore should not be read as aromaticity of every leader. N-halogen bonds occur in 635 of 870 Child proposals versus 476 of 870 Parent proposals; this chemistry did not uniformly improve merely because its incidence fell in other tasks.
liabilities: N-F and O-F occur together in the seed-0 leader. C(=O)OF is an O-F-bearing acyl hypofluorite motif, chemically distinct from an ordinary acyl fluoride C(=O)F; the related COF side chain also has an O-F bond.
Cyclopropene and unsaturation in a small aza ring raise strain concerns; the seed-1 large aromatic-labelled nitrogen ring poses a different geometry question.
The aryl hydroxylamine and terminal thiol in the seed-2 family add separate local reactivity concerns. A higher score does not certify any of these motifs as stable or drug-like.
missing_features: Stable N/O bond environments combined with credible ring geometry at comparably strong values are not demonstrated across the leading families. The N-halogen-free relative is a counterexample to an absolute requirement, but does not resolve its separate O-F and ring liabilities.

The small unsaturated rings and the large aromatic-labelled nitrogen ring lack demonstrated conformational, tautomeric and synthetic identity; graph aromatic labels and supplied scores do not provide that information.

Specified stereochemical forms are absent for substituted saturated ring centres. These trajectories identify local structural sensitivity, not a missing target-specific pharmacophore that could legally be hard-coded into the generator.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Child seed leaders score 0.5728430096095309, 0.4261398870896358 and 0.5253235827884025, below the corresponding Parent values 0.6510211907030741, 0.4870057305679067 and 0.7208853668418119. The Parent's seed-2 cyclic-cumulene family remains geometrically questionable despite its higher score; the comparison does not establish a chemically desirable missing cumulene. In Child seed 0, evaluation 293 has N-fluoromethyl substitution and scores 0.5728430096095309; the otherwise matching N-aminomethyl analogue at evaluation 297 scores 0.001478480455531148. That directly visible local contrast supports strong context sensitivity, while both molecules retain other reactive bonds. The seed-0 N-halogen-free relative at evaluation 294 still scores 0.44819844578843687, although it retains O-F and strained-ring concerns. Initial aryl fused dione scores 0.0020944534688323298, isolated F scores 1.1043196211273875e-26, and a 45-heavy-atom duplicated dione assembly scores 6.045610608603399e-17. The association is with a compact, specifically substituted fluorinated polar arrangement; fluorine alone, larger nitrogen-rich structures and generic fluorination do not reproduce it.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The indexed n-62daf219c70a report traces this gap to n-c55c3d520a2c; it is re-observed in n-aa9acd2c2043 on the supplied Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2 with 300 observations per task and batch size 10. N-halogen and O-halogen bonds appear in 975 and 147 of 4350 Child proposals, compared with 1042 and 278 in the current Parent; incidence moves in different directions between chemical families. Leading examples include N-fluoro amides, N-halogen heterocycles and O-F-bearing carbonyl groups. Other strong examples have ordinary carbon-bound halogens, and a halogen-free diaza-lactam family also appears. The liability is environment-specific, not a lack of heterocycles or amines. Historical origin and current evidence are not pooled.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve conventional local bond environments within otherwise useful aromatic and heterocyclic frameworks.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator needs transformations that distinguish carbon-bound halogens from N/O-halogen environments and offer plausible local alternatives while retaining useful scaffold and functional-group relationships learned from accepted feedback. These observations do not establish a score benefit for a blanket filter or identify which component produced the liability.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This gap is carried from n-c55c3d520a2c through the n-62daf219c70a assessment and recurs in the current n-aa9acd2c2043 Search panel at the supplied budget and profile. The Child includes cyclopropene-containing polar rings, small unsaturated aza rings, dense aromatic-labelled aza cages, large aromatic-labelled nitrogen rings and medium-ring diaryl bridges. Conventional cyclic amines also score highly. A compact pyrrolidine/indane without an extra chloro-aziridine scores 0.9999918570022562 alongside an elaborated relative at 0.9999959962849514. Difficult ring chemistry is therefore not a universal requirement for high observed values; the different historical and current profiles remain separate.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently distinguish a valid ring graph from credible unsaturation, bridging and aromatic geometry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring transformations need sensitivity to ring size, bond geometry and bridge connectivity, with feasible alternative topologies preserving useful chemical relationships. Perceived ring counts and lowercase aromatic labels cannot supply this information. This supports investigating geometric feasibility, not prohibiting all small rings or inferring score improvement or mediation.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The n-62daf219c70a report records this gap originally in n-c55c3d520a2c. It is re-observed in n-aa9acd2c2043 across the supplied Search Seeds and frozen profile: every task has stereocentre-string incidence 0.0 despite substituted pyrrolidines, indanes, small rings, medium rings and potentially stereogenic sulfoxide/carbon environments. Some leading planar or unbridged families lack such centres, so stereochemistry is a structure-dependent issue. Formal-charge incidence is also 0.0, but visible aliphatic amines make that a distinct protonation-representation question, not absent basicity.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator leaves potentially stereogenic molecular structures without specified stereochemical identity.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve or resolve stereochemistry when transformations create or modify relevant centres, treating achiral and configurationally unstable cases appropriately. Assess protonation and tautomerism separately. These data establish unspecified identity, not a measured stereochemical score penalty or a component-specific cause.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The gap originates in the n-c55c3d520a2c assessment carried by n-62daf219c70a and remains visible in n-aa9acd2c2043 under the current supplied Search panel and budget. There are 111 Child proposals with at most five heavy atoms, including late floor-scoring fragments, while enlarged duplicate-like indole-amide, dione and heterocycle assemblies can also score poorly. A 113-heavy-atom assembly scores 0.5845735884715332 below its more compact 41-heavy-atom family leader at 0.626750700280112. Conversely, the compact 19-heavy-atom cyclic-amine example remains near the supplied score ceiling. These are contextual comparisons, not a universal size rule or independent replication of historical samples.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably preserve useful functional-group context while controlling fragmentation and excessive elaboration.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Use task-local accepted feedback to learn which connected chemical context must survive a simplification, extension or scaffold replacement. The needed capability is control of context loss and unnecessary elaboration; neither a fixed size floor nor an automatic preference for larger structures follows from the evidence. An improvement in search endpoints would require its own evaluation.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This is the coverage gap traced by n-62daf219c70a to n-c55c3d520a2c, re-observed conditionally in n-aa9acd2c2043 on the current Search Seeds and budget. High-scoring aromatic amides and fluorinated diones often vary peripheral halogens or short side chains on recurring cores, and different seeds reach materially different ring families. The full output nevertheless contains many alternative topologies, and some leading amino-carbonyl families are structurally varied. Thus the observation is inconsistent useful coverage, not global collapse, inability to make rings, or proof that structural diversity declined because of this intervention.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently provide chemically independent plausible alternatives to each seed-local leading family.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Explore feasible scaffold transformations that preserve learned functional relationships while changing chemically meaningful connectivity. Assess whether the alternatives remain useful under accepted task-local feedback instead of treating distinct SMILES, ring counts or more cores as success. The source conditions remain attached to this hypothesis; neither a particular component cause nor a general score benefit is established.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

method_references.title: Austin Tripp and José Miguel Hernández-Lobato. Genetic algorithms are strong baselines for molecule generation. arXiv:2310.09267, 2023. Sections 2–3 and Appendix A describe the anchor.
method_references.citation: Austin Tripp and José Miguel Hernández-Lobato. Genetic algorithms are strong baselines for molecule generation. arXiv:2310.09267, 2023. Sections 2–3 and Appendix A describe the anchor.
method_references.supports: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
